payload.source_excerpt:
**Sets:** $I$ = elements to cover, $J$ = available sets

**Parameters:** $c_j$ = cost of set $j$; $a_{ij} = 1$ if set $j$ covers element $i$

**Variables:** $x_j \in \{0,1\}$ — select set $j$

nodes.summary: Sets: I = items, B = \{1, \ldots, |I|\} = candidate bins

payload.source_excerpt:
**Sets:** $I$ = items, $B = \{1, \ldots, |I|\}$ = candidate bins

**Parameters:** $w_i$ = item weight, $C$ = bin capacity

**Variables:** $x_{ib} \in \{0,1\}$ — item $i$ in bin $b$; $y_b \in \{0,1\}$ — bin $b$ used

**Formulation:**
$$\min \sum_{b \in B} y_b$$
$$\text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{b \in B} x_{ib} = 1 \quad \forall i \in I$$
$$\sum_{i \in I} w_i x_{ib} \leq C \cdot y_b \quad \forall b \in B$$
$$x_{ib} \in \{0,1\},\ y_b \in \{0,1\}$$

**Symmetry breaking:** $y_1 \geq y_2 \geq \cdots \geq y_{|B|}$

nodes.summary: Sets: I = customers, J = candidate facilities

payload.source_excerpt:
**Sets:** $I$ = customers, $J$ = candidate facilities

**Parameters:** $f_j$ = fixed cost, $c_{ij}$ = unit service cost, $d_i$ = demand

**Variables:** $y_j \in \{0,1\}$ open; $x_{ij} \geq 0$ fraction served

**Formulation:**
$$\min \sum_{j \in J} f_j y_j + \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{j \in J} c_{ij} d_i x_{ij}$$
$$\text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{j \in J} x_{ij} = 1 \quad \forall i \in I$$
$$x_{ij} \leq y_j \quad \forall i \in I, j \in J$$
$$y_j \in \{0,1\},\ x_{ij} \geq 0$$

**Capacitated (CFLP):** Add $\sum_{i} d_i x_{ij} \leq q_j y_j \quad \forall j$.

nodes.title: Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) — DFJ Formulation
nodes.summary: Sets: V = \{0,1,\ldots,n\} cities, E = edges

payload.source_excerpt:
**Sets:** $V = \{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ cities, $E$ = edges

**Parameters:** $c_{ij}$ = distance

**Variables:** $x_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$

**Formulation:**
$$\min \sum_{(i,j) \in E} c_{ij} x_{ij}$$
$$\text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{j:(i,j)\in E} x_{ij} = 2 \quad \forall i \in V$$
$$\sum_{i \in S, j \in S} x_{ij} \leq |S| - 1 \quad \forall S \subset V, 2 \leq |S| \leq |V|-1$$
$$x_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$$

**Note:** Subtour constraints added via lazy callback. Exponential number but manageable.

### TSP — MTZ Formulation (Compact)

Additional variables: $u_i \geq 0$ — position of city $i$ in tour

$$u_i - u_j + n \cdot x_{ij} \leq n - 1 \quad \forall i,j \in V\setminus\{0\}, i \neq j$$
$$1 \leq u_i \leq n-1 \quad \forall i \in V\setminus\{0\}$$

**Warning:** Much weaker LP relaxation than DFJ.

nodes.title: Capacitated VRP (CVRP)
nodes.summary: Sets: V = \{0\} \cup C (depot + customers), K = vehicles

payload.source_excerpt:
**Sets:** $V = \{0\} \cup C$ (depot + customers), $K$ = vehicles

**Parameters:** $c_{ij}$, $d_i$ = demand, $Q$ = vehicle capacity

**Variables:** $x_{ijk} \in \{0,1\}$ — vehicle $k$ uses arc $(i,j)$

**Formulation:**
$$\min \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{(i,j)} c_{ij} x_{ijk}$$
$$\text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{k \in K} \sum_{j} x_{ijk} = 1 \quad \forall i \in C$$
$$\sum_{j} x_{0jk} = 1 \quad \forall k \in K \quad \text{(leave depot)}$$
$$\sum_{i} x_{i0k} = 1 \quad \forall k \in K \quad \text{(return depot)}$$
$$\sum_{j} x_{ijk} - \sum_{j} x_{jik} = 0 \quad \forall i \in C, k \in K \quad \text{(flow)}$$
$$\sum_{i \in C} d_i \sum_{j} x_{ijk} \leq Q \quad \forall k \in K$$
+ subtour elimination

nodes.title: Job-Shop Scheduling (JSSP)
nodes.summary: Sets: J = jobs, M = machines; O_j = ordered operations for job j

payload.source_excerpt:
**Sets:** $J$ = jobs, $M$ = machines; $O_j$ = ordered operations for job $j$

**Parameters:** $p_{jm}$ = processing time of job $j$ on machine $m$

**Variables:** $s_{jm} \geq 0$ — start time; $z_{j_1 j_2 m} \in \{0,1\}$ — $j_1$ before $j_2$ on machine $m$; $C_{\max} \geq 0$

**Formulation:**
$$\min C_{\max}$$
$$\text{s.t.} \quad s_{j,m_{k+1}} \geq s_{j,m_k} + p_{j,m_k} \quad \forall j, \text{consecutive ops } (m_k, m_{k+1})$$
$$s_{j_1,m} \geq s_{j_2,m} + p_{j_2,m} - M(1 - z_{j_1 j_2 m}) \quad \forall j_1 \neq j_2, m$$
$$s_{j_2,m} \geq s_{j_1,m} + p_{j_1,m} - M \cdot z_{j_1 j_2 m} \quad \forall j_1 \neq j_2, m$$
$$C_{\max} \geq s_{j,m_{\text{last}}} + p_{j,m_{\text{last}}} \quad \forall j$$

**Big-M:** $M = \sum_{j \in J} \max_m p_{jm} \cdot |M|$ or tighter per-machine bound.

---

nodes.title: Flow-Shop Scheduling (FSSP — permutation)
nodes.summary: Sets: J = jobs, M = \{1,\ldots,m\} machines

payload.source_excerpt:
**Sets:** $J$ = jobs, $M = \{1,\ldots,m\}$ machines

**Parameters:** $p_{jm}$

**Variables:** $x_{jk} \in \{0,1\}$ — job $j$ in position $k$; $C_{km} \geq 0$ — completion of position $k$ on machine $m$

**Formulation:**
$$\min C_{|J|,m}$$
$$\text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{k} x_{jk} = 1 \quad \forall j \quad \text{(each job one position)}$$
$$\sum_{j} x_{jk} = 1 \quad \forall k \quad \text{(each position one job)}$$
$$C_{k,m'} \geq C_{k,m'-1} + \sum_j p_{jm'} x_{jk} \quad \forall k, m' > 1$$
$$C_{k,m'} \geq C_{k-1,m'} + \sum_j p_{jm'} x_{jk} \quad \forall k > 1, m'$$

nodes.title: Transportation Problem
nodes.summary: Sets: I = supply nodes, J = demand nodes

payload.source_excerpt:
**Sets:** $I$ = supply nodes, $J$ = demand nodes

**Parameters:** $c_{ij}$ = unit cost, $s_i$ = supply, $d_j$ = demand

**Variables:** $x_{ij} \geq 0$ (continuous — TU)

**Formulation:**
$$\min \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{j \in J} c_{ij} x_{ij}$$
$$\text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{j \in J} x_{ij} \leq s_i \quad \forall i \in I$$
$$\sum_{i \in I} x_{ij} \geq d_j \quad \forall j \in J$$
$$x_{ij} \geq 0$$

**Balance:** If $\sum s_i > \sum d_j$, supply constraints have slack. If equal, use = constraints.

nodes.title: Portfolio Optimization (Markowitz Mean-Variance)
nodes.summary: Sets: I = assets

payload.source_excerpt:
**Sets:** $I$ = assets

**Parameters:** $\mu_i$ = expected return, $\Sigma$ = covariance matrix, $r_{\min}$ = target return

**Variables:** $x_i \geq 0$ — portfolio weight

**Formulation:**
$$\min \mathbf{x}^T \Sigma \mathbf{x}$$
$$\text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{i \in I} x_i = 1$$
$$\sum_{i \in I} \mu_i x_i \geq r_{\min}$$
$$x_i \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in I$$

**Type:** Convex QP. With cardinality constraints ($\sum z_i \leq K$, $x_i \leq z_i$, $z_i \in \{0,1\}$) becomes MIQP.

payload.source_excerpt:
Choose the simplest correct class from the OBJECTIVE and CONSTRAINT algebraic form (linear vs quadratic/conic/nonlinear; continuous vs discrete), NOT from the problem name:

| Class | Boundary | Example families |
|---|---|---|
| **LP** | all linear + all continuous + total-unimodular/network/assignment (LP relaxation integral) | transportation, assignment, min-cost flow, max flow, shortest path, transshipment, circulation, bipartite matching, blending, diet, production mix |
| **Continuous convex (QP / conic / SDP)** | objective/constraints quadratic/conic/semidefinite + convex + continuous (no integer vars) | portfolio (Markowitz), convex QP, SOCP, SDP |
| **MILP** | linear objective & constraints + genuine discrete (0-1 / general-integer) decision | set cover/packing/partitioning, knapsack, bin packing, facility location, routing (TSP/VRP), scheduling, lot-sizing, graph coloring, cutting stock |
| **QIP / MIQP** | quadratic objective + discrete variables | quadratic assignment (QAP), cardinality-constrained portfolio |
| **MINLP / CP-SAT / NLP** | discrete+nonconvex-nonlinear, pure nonconvex nonlinear, or CP structure | — |

Key rules:
- A **quadratic objective over discrete variables ⇒ QIP/MIQP**, never MILP (the QAP-class error). Do not linearize a quadratic objective into redundant index-boolean products.
- A **TU / network / assignment / transportation** family needs NO integer variables (LP relaxation is integral).
- **Variable-minimality (index-as-decision-dimension):** index a variable only over independent decision dimensions. Do NOT index a flow/load variable over an extra dimension (e.g. arc × vehicle) when conservation/identical-vehicles determines that dimension. nodes.title: TU (Total Unimodularity) Rules
nodes.summary: A constraint matrix A is TU if every square submatrix has determinant in {-1, 0, 1}.

payload.source_excerpt:
A constraint matrix A is TU if every square submatrix has determinant in {-1, 0, 1}.

**Sufficient conditions (Ghouila-Houri):** Each column has at most two non-zero entries which are +1 and -1, and rows can be partitioned into two sets such that same-set entries in a column have opposite signs, different-set entries have same signs.

**Automatically TU problem classes:**

| Problem | Why TU | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| Assignment | Node-arc incidence of bipartite graph | Declare x_{ij} continuous |
| Transportation | Same structure as assignment | Declare x_{ij} continuous |
| Min-cost flow | Node-arc incidence of directed graph | Declare f_{ij} continuous |
| Max flow | Special case of min-cost flow | Declare f_{ij} continuous |
| Shortest path | Special case of min-cost flow | Declare f_{ij} continuous |

**NOT TU (must use integer/binary):**

- Set covering/partitioning (general 0-1 matrix)
- Knapsack, bin packing
- GAP (generalized assignment)
- Facility location (linking constraints break TU)
- TSP, VRP, scheduling

nodes.title: Ambiguity Detection Rules
nodes.summary: Flag as ambiguity (ask user) when:

payload.source_excerpt:
Flag as **ambiguity** (ask user) when:
1. Problem says "number of X" but X could be fractional in practice (e.g., "number of hours" — integer or continuous?)
2. Proportions that might need to be exact fractions vs approximate
3. "At most K types" — cardinality constraint needs binary indicators; confirm K

Flag as **assumption** (document and proceed) when:
4. Standard convention applies (e.g., "assign workers" implies binary)
5. TU structure makes domain choice irrelevant
6. Physical indivisibility is obvious (e.g., vehicles, people)
